readout_other: two-photon Ca2+ imaging (GCaMP6s); LFP via 16-channel microelectrode array; GFAP, Iba-1, NeuN staining 6 months after exposure
direction_notes: 40 kHz ultrasound through gel coupling increased Ca2+ signals and LFP (high-gamma) in somatosensory and auditory cortex in a tone-burst-duration-dependent way under isoflurane; responses were absent in brain slices and abolished by ketamine; no response without acoustic coupling.
safety_notes: No glial reaction or neuronal damage vs sham 6 months after a single 10% 500 us exposure; no immediate cell death or prolonged activation during imaging; authors state this is not a comprehensive safety assessment. Intracranial temperature rise under 1 degC in cadavers.

flags.reason: Table 1 gives peak-to-peak pressure 'in water' (235 kPa for 500 us bursts, 300 kPa otherwise); the paper states pressures are peak-to-peak unless noted.
PRF is paired with TBD and duty cycle in Table 1 (200, 20, 0.4 Hz at 10%; 1000, 100, 2 Hz at 50%); CW has none.
Animal and trial numbers appear only in figure panels and legends, no total is stated in the text.

A sham control was delivered in random order but its mechanism is not described; decoupling the transducer (no gel) and 12 kHz audible sound were separate comparison conditions (sound is not ultrasound and is not recorded as an exposure).
300 kPa is the in-water maximum of the 40 kHz transducer; the paper does not state where the pressure was specified for the slice setup.
Slice paradigms: in vivo parameters, then 50% DC with a 500 ms burst and CW; the 10% value is inferred from 'parameters employed in in vivo experiments' and is not separately stated for slices.
Text says total exposure 500 ms; Fig. 4 legend mentions only a 1-s exposure for the 500 kHz condition.
Burst rule: '100 ms burst duration, 50% DC, 5 bursts' read as 100 ms pulses within a 500 ms total exposure.
Maker named is Steiner & Martins (Langevin transducer); not in the closed list, so other_manufacturer.
